definition: The fact that permission, knowledge of revocations and collectible funds do not cross from one owner's machine to another's on their own, and do not cross together.
A group of harbors with different owners that exchange cards, revocations and payments while none of them rules the others.

An append-only log to which every harbor posts signed summaries of its records, so that anyone can check what a harbor published, and any auditor who receives two signed versions for the same epoch holds proof that the harbor equivocated.
The four-message exchange in which a destination harbor checks a card offered by another harbor and then issues its own card, valid only at the destination.

A daemon's exclusive authority over issuing and revoking its own harbor's cards, setting the rule for narrowing them, deciding which cards from other harbors to accept, and signing that harbor's epoch roots.
The property of an operation whose effects cross from one owner's harbor into another's.
A link whose two endpoints reconcile their reports directly, so an auditor holds a direct cross-check of it.
A link whose endpoints never reconcile it but whose two reports both reach the auditor by gossip.
A link from which no report reaches the auditor, so it constrains nothing.
The list of reported differences, one per link, that the auditor actually receives.
The list of link differences that one consistent assignment of values to the vertices would produce.
The smallest distance between the reported differences and any set of differences that one consistent assignment could produce, with severed links filled in however fits best.
A vector space of numbers at every vertex and edge of a graph, together with maps saying which of a vertex's numbers are compared along each of its edges.
The vector of numbers a cellular sheaf attaches to one vertex or edge, such as the encoding of one witness's log state.
In a sheaf model, a map that takes the data held at one place (a harbor, or a witness) to the part of it that an overlap or edge compares.
Restriction maps that keep the first few coordinates of a witness's numbers, the same block at both ends of an edge.
One assignment of data to every harbor or witness that agrees with every overlap or visible edge at once.
The set of edge vectors orthogonal to every coboundary; on a ring it is spanned by the vector that goes once around.
A small set of received reports that anyone can check and that cannot all be honest together.

With every visible link given one ohm, the voltage needed to push one ampere between an edge's endpoints through the whole network; it measures how well the rest of the network can explain away a lie on that edge.
A way of writing one of several values as a vector in which exactly one entry is one.
Endpoint values forced by a disagreement receipt, which fixes its tail to one value and its head to another.
All the coordinates carried by one channel, counted as one unit when measuring how many channels an error touches.

The fewest channels that must change to turn one honest-looking report pattern into a different honest-looking one; errors on fewer channels are detected, and errors on fewer than half as many can be located.
The four whole-bond status records (posted, in escrow, cleared, refunded), exactly one of which holds a funded bond at any time.
